--- CHUNK 1 ---
Received on the 25th of March 1741. Java's East Coast, the 20th of March 1741. From Batavia. To His Excellency the High and Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, together with the further Noble Lords, Councillors of the Dutch Indies. High and Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed, Earnest, Mighty, Wise, Prudent, Most Generous Lord, and Well-Noble Lords. In accordance with Your High and Noble, Great and Esteemed, Highly Respected order of the 2nd of this month, herewith returns the ship Enkhuijsen [Enkhuizen], laden with the remainder of 416 loads of rice and 8,000 pounds of dried pepper for Coromandel and Surat, amounting according to invoice to ƒ29,903:1 [Dutch guilders], which Your High and Noble Esteemed on Java's East Coast the 20th of March 1744 will be pleased to examine further and confirm. Also, the aforementioned vessel has arrived here safely, bringing 20,000 Rixdollars [Rd„s], for whose favorable receipt I have the honor to express my due thanks, and shall also in the future, in case Your High and Noble Great Esteemed honored petition cannot be fulfilled, have the honor to present to Your High and Noble Great Esteemed the true reasons therefor. With which this concludes under the wish for God's precious protection, as I have the honor with deep respect to be Your High and Noble, Strict, Great Esteemed Lord and Well-Noble Lords, Your High and Noble, Great Esteemed, entirely obedient and loyal servant. [was signed] Grothe. [in margin] Tagal, the 20th of March, 1741. Register of the Papers which by the ship the Lis are sent from here to Their Excellencies the High

From Java's East Coast, the 27th of March 1741. Indian Government at Batavia, namely No. 1. Original common missive to the High aforementioned Their Excellencies, written by the Noble and Esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Chief Merchant and Commander of Java's North East Coast, and the Council here, under today's date. 2. Bills of lading and invoices concerning the cargo loaded, brought by the bearer hereof. 3. Two expense accounts concerning provisions furnished to the aforementioned vessel and the ship the Pearl [de Peerel], likewise two Extract Resolutions dated the 10th and 16th of this month, taken in Council here. 4. Copy of letter by the Merchant Benjamin Blom and the Council at Surabaya sent hither, together with a project concerning the renewal of the dilapidated fortification works there, dated the 16th and 17th current. From Java's East Coast, the 27th of March 1744. 5. Copy of letter by the Under-Merchant and Rombang's Resident Zacharias de Bensin, written under date of the 17th of this month. 6. Original sealed and addressed to Their High Excellencies missive by the Palembang servants, accompanied by a pass and copy of invoice concerning

--- CHUNK 5 ---
From Java's East Coast, the 27th of March 1744. 5. Copy of letter by the Under-Merchant and Rombang's Resident Zacharias de Bensin, written under date of the 17th of this month. 6. Original sealed and addressed to Their High Excellencies missive by the Palembang servants, accompanied by a pass and copy of invoice concerning cotton yarn delivered in kind for the Government of Makassar. 7. Baeren Clouw, Secretary. Batavia. To His Excellency the High and Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor-General, and Noble Lords, Councillors of the Dutch Indies. Received on the 5th of April 1741. By the ship High Excellency missives Sorgwyk with the first administrator, whose already [uncertain: tagnsp:l] of the Company's effects departing. From Java's East Coast, the 27th of March 1748. High and Noble, Strict, Great and Esteemed, Earnest, Mighty, Wise, Prudent, Most Generous, Commanding Lords and Well-Noble Lords. The Lis. After the departure of our most recent submissive letter of the 15th of the past month of February, we have had the good fortune to receive Your High and Noble, Great and Esteemed, much honored missives of the 17th, and receipt of them, dated the 1st and 3rd of this month, with the papers mentioned therein, of which the last-mentioned bearer has been the Merchant and elected First Administrator, the arrival of Constantijn Sebens, to whom from the departing Merchant and elected First Administrator of the Island of Unrest and Kuiper Joan Gede, proper transport has been delivered of the warehouses and the Company's effects resting therein, has obtained likewise taken his seat in our political and judicial council, and stands ready to proceed with the aforementioned vessel, the cargo of the Lis, two expense accounts, speaking to the aforementioned, sent to Rembang. From Java's East Coast, the

--- CHUNK 1 ---
The arrival of Constantijn Sebens, who was appointed First Administrator by the departing merchant and First Administrator of the Islands, has brought about the proper transfer of the warehouses and the Company's effects contained therein. He has taken his seat in our political and judicial council and is prepared to proceed with the aforementioned vessel with a cargo of the ship De Lis, which was sent to Rembang on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1745. The merchant Loten is proceeding to Batavia with the ship Dorgwyk, which lies in cargo, and has properly delivered here such cash, beverages, and goods as are mentioned in the received bill of lading and invoice. For the sending of these we express our humble thanks, and we have provided the Surabaya office with its portion. Meanwhile, the bearer of this has received his cargo consisting of 280 loads of rice, 29 bales of cotton yarn, 2000 pieces of legger duijgen [uncertain: type of cloth or material], yielding ƒ19,547:16:8. As evidenced by the attached bills of lading, vessel and pearl invoice paired with two cost calculations and extracts from our aforementioned council decisions dated the 10th and 16th of this month, it appears that the ship De Lis received provisioning, arrack, and further refreshment for its sick crew members, just as the ship De Peer received the same. The two last-mentioned vessels, being the aforementioned vessel which was sent to Rembang to receive its cargo, amounting to the sums of ƒ400:9:8 and ƒ230:5, which amounts we humbly renew the request made by the resident for spikes and bar iron on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1741. From requests to be allowed to deduct from the trade books, and let this further serve as a guide with the concluded copy of the letter written by the Surabaya officials, together with a project in duplicate dated the 16th and 17th of the aforementioned month, whereby it was requested

--- CHUNK 2 ---
to receive the cargo amounting to the sums of ƒ400:9:8 and ƒ230:5, which amounts we humbly renew the request made by the resident for spikes and bar iron on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1741. From requests to be allowed to deduct from the trade books, and let this further serve as a guide with the concluded copy of the letter written by the Surabaya officials, together with a project in duplicate dated the 16th and 17th of the aforementioned month, whereby it was requested for permission to renew the mostly deteriorated Surabaya works according to their assessment, the costs of which would amount to a sum of ƒ39,862:15:—, which petition we present in all humility to Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority], just as also that by renewal of the under-merchant and Rembang's resident Zacharias de Bensin made by a letter from Rembang, a copy of which is annexed, dated the 13th, in order to be able to enjoy what is cited in our letter of the 15th before, namely, 4000 six-inch spikes and what bar iron of three-quarter inch for the use of the six requested chaloups [small boats], the mills being also brought into readiness for Japara, while the 4 pant chiallings [uncertain: type of vessel or measurement] already lie at our disposal. Here we also enclose an original letter concerning the dwelling, which was from the officials at Palembang on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1744, accompanied by a pass certificate showing that for the Company's account here were delivered 1000 pieces of cadjan mats [woven palm leaf mats] by the Sumanap per Tertauwidjaja, which after his residence, due to lack of the vessel, was returned, which volume we shall use the freedom to send to Batavia at the first opportunity, since the same cannot be employed here, while this is further accompanied by a copy of an invoice of cotton yarn in kind delivered for the government of Macassar, amounting to guilders

--- CHUNK 3 ---
a pass certificate showing that for the Company's account here were delivered 1000 pieces of cadjan mats by the Sumanap per Tertauwidjaja, which after his residence, due to lack of the vessel, was returned, which volume we shall use the freedom to send to Batavia at the first opportunity, since the same cannot be employed here, while this is further accompanied by a copy of an invoice of cotton yarn in kind delivered for the government of Macassar, amounting to guilders ƒ1,096:10:8, and paired with various lists of passes from Rembang, Surabaya, and here provided to Batavia on the 2nd of January, February, and up to the present date, various Chinese [merchants]. Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority] will also have debtors, and it will please you to order that the Secretary's accounting on behalf of the council of Justice here, for the benefit of the chief merchant and Secretary of the esteemed Council of Justice of the Castle Batavia, Gysbertus Schuijlenburg, would seize such monies as the Chinese residing here on the east coast of Java on the 21st of March 1744, namely Ni Ponko, Ni Tjanko, Ni Goanko, and Gouw Tsoko, would owe as authorized agents to their principal, the detained Captain Ni Toekong and his brother Nclienkong, who is in custody. This, just as the orders of Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority] by letter of the 19th of December last, as confirmed, concern the aforementioned and several other Chinese mentioned in the received petitions. With due obedience this has been followed, yet since these people in these troubled times cannot be properly constrained to swift payment, we have not been able to proceed further with this, and thus for now we have only recorded what they properly acknowledge to be owing to the aforementioned Captain Nihoekong and his brothers Nr. Lienkong, Ni Tweskong, and Nihoekong, consisting of N. Tseeko owing to Nielien Long rds

--- CHUNK 4 ---
other Chinese mentioned in the received petitions. With due obedience this has been followed, yet since these people in these troubled times cannot be properly constrained to swift payment, we have not been able to proceed further with this, and thus for now we have only recorded what they properly acknowledge to be owing to the aforementioned Captain Nihoekong and his brothers Nr. Lienkong, Ni Tweskong, and Nihoekong, consisting of N. Tseeko owing to Nielien Long rds 800. Captain Niekae Kong: 3000. N Tsaangko Ni Simko. Nietsjetkongn: 5000. Cast Niehoekong: 5000. Ni Ponko. Transported rds 13,800. The demand for rice shall be fulfilled with all diligence. On the rice harvest the sugar is scarce on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1744. Per Transport R. dos 13,800. Nihoan Ko owing to Nie Hoekong: 1800. Ni Goanko owing to Nighoangkong: 5800. Kohoet and owing to Nihoekong: 6800. Gdutotsoko still not appeared from Rembang, will be the payment per further occasion given, amounting to Rds 27,400. Which sum we shall endeavor to collect according to our ability. Meanwhile, we note in the continuation of this that Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority] has made demands for sugar and demands for sugar and rice, which with all care are being striven to be fulfilled. But since the rice harvest, due to the unsettled weather, cannot yet be calculated, we shall have the honor at the proper time to communicate the price thereof, being until further notice the sugar in that quantity cannot be calculated as thought, not delivered, in view of the fact that many sugar mills in these troubles on Java have not been properly maintained, so that this commodity is dearer than in previous years when

--- CHUNK 5 ---
the rice harvest, due to the unsettled weather, cannot yet be calculated, we shall have the honor at the proper time to communicate the price thereof, being until further notice the sugar in that quantity cannot be calculated as thought, not delivered, in view of the fact that many sugar mills in these troubles on Java have not been properly maintained, so that this commodity is dearer than in previous years when the same was purchased before the uprising of the Chinese in Batavia, and is daily rising. On the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1741, the price here of the first sort is no less than 4½ and the second for 4 42ds [uncertain: unit of measurement or currency], to be obtained, provided that the Company bears the costs falling upon the delivery thereof, and it also continues to rise daily, so we humbly request that if it becomes dearer, Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority] will be pleased to qualify us for this purchase, and then to be provided with the necessary cash therefor. And besides this, a demand for cash of a sum of 30,000 rds [rixdollars: Spanish silver coins], because the cash here is already 12,000 Rds behind, due to the payment of the purchased 1000 loads of rice in a[nno] pass[ato] and other products, for which no money has yet been received, except that to satisfy the anticipated needs per indigo, cotton yarn, and also to assist the outer offices, the remaining 18,000 rds will still be needed for the receipt of the general demand, which we, in accordance with the order, as soon as possible to Your High Noble and Greatly Esteemed [authority], shall forward, being here still also in the cash the regulation regarding the Company service taking of the inland obligated obedience on the east coast of Java on the 27th of March 1741. A sum of 900

--- CHUNK 1 ---
seen by way of Indigo, Cotton yarn & likewise the assistance of the outer Comptoirs, the remaining 18,000 rixdollars [modern equivalent: Dutch East India Company currency] will still be needed for the receipt of the general Requisition which we, in accordance with the order, as soon as possible shall forward to Your High Noble great esteemed [person], there being here still at the Cash office the regulation concerning the Company service taking of the Inland owed obedience from Java's east coast on the 27th of March 1741. A sum of 900 [uncertain: possibly 2r0o] in copper duyten [modern equivalent: small Dutch coins], but since the uprising of the Chinese we have not been able to exchange them here at the Coast. The received regulation regarding children, likewise concerning the taking on of Inland [persons], shall be observed. Children in the service of the Esteemed Company shall with due observance be followed, shall be with respect to their age and merits, with which with deep respect I remain [understood] High Noble Stern widely commanding Lord and well Noble gentlemen [lower] Your High Noble great esteemed [person] very entirely your obedient and obedient Servants [was signed]. B[artholomeus] Visscher R[udolph] E[von] van Glan Joan Gideon Loten, Constantijn Piebens, G. Request from the ship the Lis [normalized version: de Lis] lying at this roadstead, skipper Willem van Loon, reading thus: To the Esteemed Noble Gentlemen, Lord Bartholomeus Visscher chief merchant and governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the Council Esteemed Noble Gentlemen and Lords. Willem van Loon, skipper of the ship the Lis lying at this roadstead, to Your Esteemed Noble Gentlemen humbly gives to know that the outer seams above water as well as the deck seams within the aforesaid bottom have so warped that before they are caulked no rice or other products that are subject to spoilage can be loaded, wherefore the Supplicant humbly requests that the aforesaid seams by the honored command of your esteemed [person] may be made tight, as also from Java's East Coast under date 27th of March 1741. In order to be able to enjoy some further

--- CHUNK 3 ---

In order to be able to enjoy some further provisions and arrack [modern equivalent: a type of distilled spirit] as ration for the sailing crew members [understood] which doing &c., so it is after the foregoing careful deliberation that the request being justly judged, it was unanimously decided to consent thereto, and likewise to give respectful notice thereof to their Excellencies the high government of the Netherlands India at Batavia [understood] For P[ieter] Accorded [was signed] I L[...] their Clerk Secretary Thursday the 16th of March 1741 in the forenoon at 9 o'clock. Present the chief merchant and governor of this Coast Bartholomeus Visscher, the Captain Rudolph Care [uncertain: possibly Carelyon] von Glan, the merchant and first administrator Joan Gideon Loten, the Lieutenant Gerrit Hendrik Alephelt, the under merchant and salary bookkeeper Pieter de Vos, and the under merchant and fiscal Jeronimus Tonnemans Junior, Deputy the under merchant and second administrator Stevenmarcus van der Heyden. Copy from Java's east coast under date 27th of March 1741 concerning Indisposition. Read being a request from the ship the Pearl [normalized version: de Peerl] lying here at the roadstead, skipper Willem Vroom, reading thus: To the Esteemed Noble Gentlemen, Lord Bartholomeus Visscher chief merchant and governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the Council Esteemed Noble Gentlemen and Lords. Willem Vroom, skipper of the ship the Pearl lying at this roadstead, to Your Esteemed Noble Gentlemen humbly requests very humbly, since many of his crew members are sick, through the goodness of Your esteemed [person] to be able to be

--- CHUNK 4 ---
lying here at the roadstead, skipper Willem Vroom, reading thus: To the Esteemed Noble Gentlemen, Lord Bartholomeus Visscher chief merchant and governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the Council Esteemed Noble Gentlemen and Lords. Willem Vroom, skipper of the ship the Pearl lying at this roadstead, to Your Esteemed Noble Gentlemen humbly requests very humbly, since many of his crew members are sick, through the goodness of Your esteemed [person] to be able to be provided with some distribution of arrack [modern equivalent: a type of distilled spirit], as it being from Batavia, without enjoying [it] having departed hither. Which doing &c., so it is after the foregoing deliberation that the request being justly judged, it was Unanimously from Java's East Coast under date 27th of March 1741 decided to consent thereto. Samarang in Council date aforesaid [was signed] B[artholomeus] Visscher R[udolph] C[are] von Gean Ioan Gedeon Loten, G[errit] H[endrik] Alephelt P[ieter] d Vos, and J[eronimus] Tonneman Junior [understood] Accorded [was signed] P[ieter] Pd Baarenelour Secretary. Samarang. To the Esteemed Noble Gentlemen Lord Bartholomeus Visscher chief merchant and Governor of Java's Northeast Coast together with the Council. Title. By return of the Sergeant Dirk Roelofs [and] 3 two soldiers, on the 20th of December of the past year, we have honored ourselves with Your Esteemed Noble [person] always respected letter of the 15th before, and thereby the requested documents of increase in wages which to the interested parties under their thanks expressed to Your Esteemed Noble [person] have been given, are with 2 months' pay at [uncertain: possibly "uso" - a commercial term]. --- CHUNK 1 ---
From Java's East Coast under date 27 May 1741, it was decided therein to consent. Semarang in Council, dated as aforesaid, was signed B. Visscher, R.C. von Gean, Ioan Gedeon Loten, G.H. Alephelt, P. de Vos, and J.s Tonneman Junior. Undersigned. Agreed, was signed P.r P.d. Baarenelour, Secretary of Semarang. To the Honored and Esteemed Lord Bartholomeus Visscher, Chief Merchant and Governor of Java's East Coast, together with the Council. Title. By return of Sergeant Dirk Roelofs. The two soldiers who departed on the 20th of December of the past year, we have found ourselves honored with Your Honored and Esteemed, always respected letter of the 15th before, and thereby the requested documents of salary increase, which have been delivered to the interested parties under their expression of thanks to Your Honored and Esteemed, are with 2 months' pay at uso [uncertain: original term]. And we likewise do so for the received writing materials. Meanwhile, from Java's East Coast under date 27 March 1741, further served by Sergeant Ambrosius Klein, together with the soldiers Gerrit van Stralen and Jan Vreugdenburg, as escort of a Roll of Servants, which humbly request the customary provision on account of the winning month's money for the first term of this current account year, under which the officers, chief surgeon, and translator, so that the same may be enjoyed in cash, annexed with a requisition of clothing—to which requiring, with a receipt roll regarding the distributions made to the Company's garrisons, accompanied by a notation of the recent journey of the Susuhunan, regarding which this Office was supplied by the Maduras Pangerang Adepattij Tsjacraningrat, the regents of this place and those of the strand and inner upper lands, paired with a copy notation of the powder supply held here, together with the number, weight, and inscription of the barrels in which the same is contained. Besides a threefold General petition of the yearly needed supplies, so far as

--- CHUNK 2 ---
distributions made to the Company's garrisons, accompanied by a notation of the recent journey of the Susuhunan, regarding which this Office was supplied by the Maduras Pangerang Adepattij Tsjacraningrat, the regents of this place and those of the strand and inner upper lands, paired with a copy notation of the powder supply held here, together with the number, weight, and inscription of the barrels in which the same is contained. Besides a threefold General petition of the yearly needed supplies, so far as this as well as the Office Pasuruan with such catalogs of medicines which are likewise required, and to whose storage according to Bill of Lading, Java's East Coast under date 27 March 1741, two chests with empty pots, ampules, and bottles have been transferred, upon which we hope through the goodness of their High Excellencies to obtain satisfaction, requesting to that end a favorable advancement from Your Honored and Esteemed, as well as that the aforementioned their High Noble and Esteemed Excellencies may be respectfully presented with a specification or design regarding Carpentry and Repairs (this double included) here according to attached Copy Report of Expressly Commissioned [persons], dated 19 December aforesaid, which needs to be done. Namely, renewal of the palisading on the land side of the west point and that on the side of the east side of the Company's fortress, as well as two warehouses on the east and west side within the same, under which is included the Trading Office, meeting hall, Lodgings of the Officers, guard houses, Kitchen of the military. Item, the corner palisades, curtains, and painter's houses, together with the wooden posts and bamboo structures, covered with atap [a type of palm thatch], military guard houses on the east-west barriers, also the Stone wall or Line, from Java's East Coast under date 7 March 1741. And the Shed of the seafarers and craftsmen, made of wooden posts and bamboo and covered with atap, since the aforementioned Line has fallen in for a great part, and all the rest so by the white

--- CHUNK 3 ---
military. Item, the corner palisades, curtains, and painter's houses, together with the wooden posts and bamboo structures, covered with atap, military guard houses on the east-west barriers, also the Stone wall or Line, from Java's East Coast under date 7 March 1741. And the Shed of the seafarers and craftsmen, made of wooden posts and bamboo and covered with atap, since the aforementioned Line has fallen in for a great part, and all the rest so by the white ants consumed and by Age worm-eaten and decayed, that a total collapse threatens, just as also the Company's hospital, whereby the same requires a notable repair, since its foundations and all the walls have separated from one another through the sinking and cracking of the ground, and the surrounding walls have already fallen away in part. The one and the other would, according to Exact calculation, come to cost ƒ 39,862:15— [modern equivalent: Dutch guilders], under which reckoned that which now, as aforesaid, is merely of bamboo, must also be made strong of stone and covered with tiles, so that the Company might enjoy the required service from it for a long time. Meanwhile, it is further humbly requested of Your Honored and Esteemed that in place of the palisading laid down here a year ago, the Hope [uncertain: possibly a ship name or facility name] this Office may be provided with another and two more such small vessels, so that upon occurring occasions they may be employed. From Java's East Coast under date 27 March 1741. Finally, it serves to notify Your Honored and Esteemed that the guardians of the Sumanap's chief Regent Radeen Tommongong T. Sacranagara, Radeen Ajoe Soeradinin-grat, and her husband Radeen Aria Soera Dieningrat, with their retinue, on the 30th of the aforementioned month of January, arrived here from Semarang, and on the 4th of the current [month] undertook the journey again to Sumanap, whereby we remain with much respect. Undersigned. Title. Lower. Your Honored and Esteemed

27 March 1741. Finally, it serves to notify Your Honored and Esteemed that the guardians of the Sumanap's chief Regent Radeen Tommongong T. Sacranagara, Radeen Ajoe Soeradinin-grat, and her husband Radeen Aria Soera Dieningrat, with their retinue, on the 30th of the aforementioned month of January, arrived here from Semarang, and on the 4th of the current [month] undertook the journey again to Sumanap, whereby we remain with much respect. Undersigned. Title. Lower. Your Honored and Esteemed very obedient Servants. Was signed: B. Blom, J.n Sergeois, J.H. Krap, Noag Obree, and G. v. der Hoek. Three. In margin: Surabaya, the 17 February, Year 1741. Undersigned. Agrees. Was signed: E.l Beiren Clouw, Secretary. G. Specification of such carpentry works and materials, iron and nails in kind, etc., as would be needed according to calculation for the renewal of the old and completely dilapidated palisading on the land side of the west point and that on the east side of the Company's fortress, as well as the making of two new warehouses on the east and west side within the same, under which is included the Trading Office, meeting hall, Lodgings of the officers, guard and Kitchen of the military, which has been consumed by the 300 p——„225„ from Java's East Coast under date 27 March 1741. White ants consumed and decayed, as well as the east and west barriers with its Line, so far as the same has fallen open, as also its guard houses, gates, curtains, and painter's houses, likewise the Shed for the Seafarers and craftsmen, which stand erected of wooden posts and bamboo and covered with atap, to make the same anew of stone and cover with tiles. Item, the required repair to the Company's hospital, which foundation and all the walls have separated through the sinking and cracking of the ground and have become dilapidated, also its surrounding walls and

--- CHUNK 5 ---
guard houses, gates, curtains, and painter's houses, likewise the Shed for the Seafarers and craftsmen, which stand erected of wooden posts and bamboo and covered with atap, to make the same anew of stone and cover with tiles. Item, the required repair to the Company's hospital, which foundation and all the walls have separated through the sinking and cracking of the ground and have become dilapidated, also its surrounding walls and completely collapsed, according to written report of Lieutenant Jan Herman Krap and Ensign Noag Obree, in the presence of the Carpenter Melchior Thomasz., and before the Under-Merchant and Administrator Jan Pergedis, dated 19 September last past. For which reason it is very humbly requested that permission may be obtained for the one and the other through the Goodness of his Excellency the High Noble Lord Adriaan Valckenier, Governor General, and the Noble Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies.
